source.citation: Hussien AA, Knell R, Wunderli SL, et al. Mechanical gating of tendon fibrogenic transcription in systemic sclerosis. Nature Communications. 2026;17:3893.

experimental_root.system: 3D collagen tendon-like constructs containing tendon-derived stromal cells
experimental_root.physical_intervention: compliant versus rigid cantilever boundary conditions vary static matrix tension while holding bulk collagen material properties constant
experimental_root.mechanical_measurement: online post-deflection/traction-force readout over hours to days
experimental_root.causal_observation: rigid/high-tension boundaries increased cellular traction and promoted alpha-SMA-associated myofibroblast phenoconversion relative to compliant boundaries
experimental_root.important_nonmonotonic_result: high tension increased alpha-SMA but decreased Col1a1/Col3a1 transcription and tenogenic markers in the reductionist construct; a simple MORE_TENSION_EQUALS_MORE_COLLAGEN_TRANSCRIPTION rule is rejected.
experimental_root.immune_override: macrophage co-culture can override tension-dependent suppression of matrix-gene expression, showing that mechanics is not an isolated universal master variable.

janus_classification.reason: Mechanical state is imposed from construct formation rather than retuned after an established endogenous repair/fibrotic state, and there is no delayed in-vivo tissue repair/integrity outcome.

next_action: Search for tendon injury experiments that mechanically retune an already-established scar/adhesion state and then measure mechanics, lineage/state trajectory, function and structural integrity in the same root.
